common_name: Fragrant Cloud Skimmia (Male Pollinator Evergreen Shrub)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, acidic, humus-rich soil in shade to partial shade; this male form is grown chiefly for its intensely scented spring flowers rather than for berries.

directions: Site in humus-rich, evenly moist, well-drained acidic soil in partial to full shade, where Fragrant Cloud holds a dense, low, rounded dome of aromatic dark-green leaves. In early spring it opens creamy buds into heavily perfumed white flower clusters that can scent an entire shaded patio or entryway, and as a male selection it also serves as a reliable pollinator for female cultivars such as Rubella or Kew Green growing within several feet. It carries the RHS Award of Garden Merit and tolerates deep shade and wind better than most broadleaf evergreens, making it useful in courtyards and containers as well as woodland borders. Water during dry spells, mulch to hold soil moisture and acidity, and prune only lightly after flowering to maintain its neat habit.

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade; unlike most Skimmia, Temptation carries both sexes on one plant and sets fruit without a separate pollinator.

directions: Grow in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, acidic soil in partial shade to full shade, where glossy elliptic leaves release a light citrus scent when brushed or crushed. Temptation is a hermaphroditic Skimmia japonica selection bred in 2005, meaning a single plant flowers and fruits reliably on its own, unlike older cultivars that require separate male and female shrubs; small white spring flowers are followed by heavy clusters of shiny red berries that persist through much of winter. Its compact, vigorous, rounded habit suits foundation plantings, woodland edges, and mixed shade borders where dependable winter color is wanted without the space for two shrubs. Keep soil consistently moist but not waterlogged, mulch annually, and prune only minimally to remove damaged growth.
sources: Gardens by the Bay plant records

common_name: Winter Gem Sweet Box (Hillier Hybrid Sarcococca)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in shade to partial shade; this Hillier Nurseries hybrid of S. hookeriana and S. humilis forms an unusually dense, glossy dome.

directions: Plant in moist but well-drained, moderately fertile, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, where Winter Gem forms an upright, densely branched mound of exceptionally glossy dark-green foliage. Bred by Peter Moore at Hillier Nurseries by hand-crossing Sarcococca hookeriana with S. hookeriana var. humilis, it produces red-tinted buds that open to intensely honey-vanilla-scented white flowers from December into March, followed by black berries. Its tighter, more uniform habit than the straight species makes it well suited to foundation plantings, entry walks, and underplanting beneath deciduous trees where winter fragrance at close range is valued. Established plants tolerate dry shade and root competition, need little supplemental water once settled, and require pruning only to remove wayward stems.

common_name: Fragrant Valley Sweet Box (Compact Groundcover Sarcococca)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in deep to partial shade; this Canadian patented selection stays low and spreads evenly, making it useful as a fragrant groundcover.

directions: Site in humus-rich, evenly moist, well-drained soil in deep to partial shade; Fragrant Valley is a patented, uniform Canadian introduction that stays notably low and wide compared to the species, making it valuable as a fragrant, deer-resistant evergreen groundcover or low informal hedge beneath trees. Small white flowers open in late winter and perfume the surrounding air with the classic sweet-box vanilla-honey scent, followed by small black fruit in early summer. Because plants grow to a very consistent size, it can be mass-planted without the shaping or selective pruning other Sarcococca often need. Once established it is drought tolerant in shade and essentially pest-free; water during extended dry spells and mulch to maintain even soil moisture.

common_name: Dragon Gate Sweet Box (Arching Chinese Fragrant Sarcococca)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in shade; this Roy Lancaster collection from Yunnan is more compact and gracefully arching than the species.

directions: Grow in moderately fertile, moist but well-drained, humus-rich soil in shade to partial shade, where Dragon Gate forms a low, arching mound of fine, uniform, deep-green pointed foliage. Collected by plantsman Roy Lancaster in Yunnan, China in 1980 near the Dragon Gate temple for which it is named, this Sarcococca ruscifolia selection is more compact and gracefully weeping than the wild species, reaching only about two feet tall. Powerfully fragrant, cream-white flowers cluster on the undersides of the arching stems from midwinter into early spring, followed by red berries in summer, and the plant holds the RHS Award of Garden Merit. It tolerates dry shade and root competition once established, needs minimal supplemental water, and rarely requires pruning beyond removing damaged wood.
